answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before earning rewards or voting. During probation, peers verify useful, independent work; if evidence shows linked accounts colluding, a challenge can slash their deposits. This does not stop every Sybil, but each added identity ties up more capital and risks losing it, making mass impersonation costly. The attacker must keep each account above the ledge of review as the tide of scrutiny rises, rather than minting a costless relic of a name.
